question: Do sentiment scores from Wikipedia critical-reception sections improve closing-risk and next-week gross forecasts over numeric features alone?
method: VADER lexicon sentiment (vaderSentiment) per sentence of each article's critical-reception section, after removing sentences about box office, closings, awards or ticket sales
attribution: Scores derived from the linked English Wikipedia articles, by Wikipedia contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0. Only derived scores are stored.
limitations: Wikipedia reception sections are written or edited after opening, often after a run ends, so even with outcome sentences removed the text may reflect hindsight (look-ahead leakage). Any lift is an upper bound on what opening-night reviews would provide.
Only shows with a matched English Wikipedia article and a reception section are included, which over-represents notable productions.
Sentiment is a static per-show score; it cannot explain week-to-week changes.
VADER is a general-purpose lexicon, not tuned to theatre criticism.
